issues.legal_issue: Specific performance may be granted to the extent of the contracting co-owners’ undivided shares even when the other co-owners did not join the agreement.
material_facts: The agreement to sell was executed by some, but not all, of the co-owners.
The property was jointly owned, and the agreement provided for a conveyance of absolute title, including by having other persons join if necessary.
The seller co-owners’ interests were capable of being transferred, although the non-contracting co-owners disputed the transaction.
The purchaser sought specific performance and was willing to accept the contracting co-owners’ shares.
issues.conclusion: The decree for specific performance to the extent of the contracting co-owners’ shares was not disturbed; the purchaser was not entitled to specific performance of the entire property.
issues.legal_principle: Under the equitable principle applied in Kartar Singh v. Harjinder Singh, Sardar Singh v. Krishna Devi, A. Abdul Rashid Khan v. P.A.K.A. Shahul Hamid, Surinder Singh v. Kapoor Singh, and Gajara Vishnu Gosavi v. Prakash Nanasaheb Kamble, an agreement made by a co-owner can be specifically enforced to the extent of that co-owner’s share even if other co-owners did not join. Section 44 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, is consistent with transfer of an undivided interest. Article 2177 of the Portuguese Civil Code, 1867, does not prohibit alienation of an undivided interest; a purchaser of such an interest may seek partition, but cannot obtain possession of a specified part before partition.

rule.if: specific_performance_case and property_jointly_owned and contracting_coowner_agreed_to_sell_share and other_coowners_did_not_join

predicates.specific_performance_case: The proceeding seeks enforcement of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.property_jointly_owned: The property is owned by more than one co-owner.
predicates.contracting_coowner_agreed_to_sell_share: One or more co-owners agreed to sell their interests in the property.
predicates.other_coowners_did_not_join: One or more co-owners whose interests were also in the property did not join the agreement.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance proceeding concerns jointly owned property and only some co-owners agreed to sell, enforcement may be limited to those co-owners’ shares.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser may enforce an agreement to sell when the purchaser performs an agreed obligation to clear an encumbrance, the title obstacle is thereby removed, and the vendors nevertheless fail to complete the sale.
material_facts: The agreement required the vendors to make out good and marketable title and allowed them to have other persons join the conveyance or redeem an encumbrance.
The agreement allowed the purchaser to elect specific performance if the vendors failed to complete the sale after title was made out.
The vendors induced the purchaser to pay the outstanding mortgage liability on the understanding that the sale would then be completed.
The purchaser paid the liability, the mortgage was redeemed and the charge released, but the vendors did not complete the conveyance.
The purchaser consistently sought specific performance.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was enforceable after the mortgage was redeemed and clear title was made out, and the purchaser’s election to seek specific performance was upheld to the extent of the contracting vendors’ shares.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the terms of the agreement, particularly its provision allowing specific performance after title was made out, and its equitable assessment of the parties’ conduct. It relied on the purchaser’s continued readiness and willingness and held that vendors who induced the purchaser to discharge the mortgage on an understanding that the sale would follow could not then refuse completion.

rule.if: specific_performance_case and contract_requires_clear_title and purchaser_cleared_encumbrance_at_vendors_request and title_obstacle_removed and vendors_failed_to_complete and purchaser_elected_specific_performance

predicates.specific_performance_case: The proceeding seeks enforcement of an agreement to sell.
predicates.contract_requires_clear_title: The agreement makes completion conditional on the vendors establishing good and marketable title.
predicates.purchaser_cleared_encumbrance_at_vendors: The purchaser paid an outstanding liability secured against the property after the vendors sought or induced that payment.
predicates.title_obstacle_removed: The payment removed the encumbrance that had prevented clear title.
predicates.vendors_failed_to_complete: The vendors did not complete the sale after the title obstacle was removed.
predicates.purchaser_elected_specific_performance: The purchaser chose to seek completion of the sale rather than merely repayment or damages.

issues.definition: If the purchaser clears an encumbrance at the vendors’ request, the title obstacle is removed, and the vendors still fail to complete after the purchaser elects enforcement, the agreement may be enforced by specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: A claimed right of pre-emption is unavailable where the claimant, despite liberty to pursue the claim, does not exercise it and later deals with the disputed property.
material_facts: The co-owner claimed a right of pre-emption under the applicable succession law.
After a court proceeding concerning redemption of the mortgage, the co-owner had liberty to pursue any rights in the property according to law.
The co-owner did not pursue the claim within the period contemplated by the court’s decision and later sold the property.
The parties’ conduct also included allowing the property to face a bank sale rather than taking steps to preserve their claimed interests.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the co-owners had no available right of pre-emption in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Applying the conduct-based and equitable reasoning in the judgment to the claimed right under Portuguese law, the Court held that the co-owners’ failure to pursue the right after being given liberty to do so, together with their subsequent conduct, meant that no right of pre-emption remained available.

rule.if: property_dispute_involving_claimed_preemption and claimant_given_liberty_to_pursue_right and claimant_did_not_pursue_right and claimant_later_dealt_with_property

predicates.property_dispute_involving_claimed_preem: The proceeding concerns a disputed property over which a person claims a right of pre-emption.
predicates.claimant_given_liberty_to_pursue_right: A court or other proceeding leaves the claimant at liberty to pursue the claimed property right according to law.
predicates.claimant_did_not_pursue_right: The claimant takes no timely step to pursue the claimed right after that liberty is given.
predicates.claimant_later_dealt_with_property: The claimant later sells or otherwise deals with the disputed property.

issues.definition: A claimed pre-emption right is unavailable where its claimant is given liberty to pursue it, does not do so, and later deals with the property.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court should not interfere under Article 136 with an equitable specific-performance decree where the record shows no grave injustice warranting intervention.
material_facts: The matter came before the Court in appeals under Article 136 against a decree granting specific performance to the extent of the contracting co-owners’ shares.
The purchaser had throughout been ready and willing to perform its obligations.
The property was not readily capable of valuation, and the parties could not state its present market value.
The purchaser paid a substantial amount to discharge the mortgage and avert the bank’s sale of the property.
The Court found that no substantial or grave injustice had been caused to the appellants.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the High Court’s decree and dismissed the appeals, including the purchaser’s appeal seeking the entire property.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 confers discretionary jurisdiction, and the Court may decline to interfere where the justice of the case does not require intervention. The Court relied on Taherakhatoon (D) by Lrs. v. Salambin Mohammad and considered the purchaser’s readiness and willingness, the difficulty of valuing the property, the discharge of the mortgage, and the absence of grave injustice.

rule.if: article_136_appeal and equitable_specific_performance_decree and purchaser_ready_and_willing and purchaser_removed_property_encumbrance and no_grave_injustice_found

predicates.article_136_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal invoking the Supreme Court’s discretionary jurisdiction.
predicates.equitable_specific_performance_decree: The challenged decree grants specific performance as equitable relief.
predicates.purchaser_ready_and_willing: The purchaser consistently demonstrates readiness and willingness to perform its obligations.
predicates.purchaser_removed_property_encumbrance: The purchaser pays or otherwise clears an encumbrance affecting the property.
predicates.no_grave_injustice_found: The Court finds that declining to disturb the decree would cause no substantial or grave injustice.

issues.definition: In an appeal invoking discretionary jurisdiction, the Court may leave an equitable specific-performance decree undisturbed when the purchaser was ready and willing, removed an encumbrance, and no grave injustice is found.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who acquires property with knowledge of pending litigation does not obtain an equitable advantage over the litigating parties.
material_facts: The property was the subject of pending litigation when it was sold to the subsequent purchaser.
The subsequent purchaser knew of the litigation and of the uncertainty concerning its outcome.
The Court described the purchaser as having knowingly purchased property under litigation.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent purchaser was not entitled to equities against the purchaser seeking specific performance, and the transfer remained subject to the result of the pending proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle of lis pendens to the circumstances, holding that a transfer made while litigation concerning the property is pending is subject to the result of that litigation. The Court also relied on the purchaser’s admitted knowledge of the disputes in concluding that it had no equitable claim.

predicates.property_litigation_pending_at_transfer: A proceeding concerning rights in the property is pending when the property is transferred.
predicates.transferee_knew_of_litigation: The transferee knows about the pending proceeding when acquiring the property.

issues.definition: A transfer made during pending property litigation is subject to its outcome, and a transferee with knowledge of that litigation gains no equitable advantage.

issues.legal_issue: A civil contempt petition must be dismissed where the alleged contemnors’ conduct is not contemptuous.
material_facts: A civil contempt petition was filed in connection with the appeals.
The Court found no contemptuous conduct on the part of the alleged contemnors.
issues.legal_principle: The Court dismissed the petition after finding no contemptuous conduct on the part of the alleged contemnors.

predicates.civil_contempt_proceeding: The proceeding is a petition alleging civil contempt.
predicates.no_contemptuous_conduct_found: The Court finds that the alleged contemnors did not engage in contemptuous conduct.

issues.definition: A civil contempt petition is dismissed when the Court finds no contemptuous conduct.
